regime_context: The detector shows a trend-discipline regime where the absolute-trend gate has historically helped control drawdown on the US market (gate_helps true), eligibility is narrowing (45% of themes eligible), and leadership is concentrated in AI Infrastructure and energy-linked themes. Cross-sectional momentum rank is display-only per the backtest verdict, and the rotation headroom is small (margin 0.185, absorption 0.31), so this is a stay-with-confirmed-trends environment rather than a predictive one. No hard catalyst is provided by the macro_narrative, whose unscheduled_share is coincident context only.
emerging_watch: Watch whether AI Infrastructure's leadership (rank 1, score 1.56) handsoff to the energy complex: the energy challenger has durability 0.62 vs AI's 0.5 and three times the breadth (0.636 vs 0.125), so I am watching for the rotation margin between AI Infra and Energy Complex to go negative (energy score exceeding AI infra score) on the next detector snapshot — that condition would confirm a leadership handoff worth acting on, not just flagging.

theses.subject: US Energy Complex
theses.thesis: Energy Complex is the highest-scoring eligible theme behind AI Infrastructure, but unlike the leader it combines the eligibility gate with meaningfully broad participation (breadth 0.636) and a stronger durability bar (0.62), suggesting the trend is supported by flow rather than a single crowded name. Note that Energy (Equal-Weight) ranks just behind at #4 with breadth 0.571 and durability 0.65, reinforcing the theme's standing; I treat the two energy entries as the same underlying dynamic and express the lean through the ETF proxy.
theses.dissent: Energy breadth may be lifting because the whole complex is sensitive to the same macro factor (oil price), so 'breadth' overstates dispersion and a single supply/demand headline could reverse the entire basket at once.

falsifier.text: XLE closes below its own 50-day moving average for five consecutive sessions before the check-by date

theses.subject: Cybersecurity
theses.thesis: Cybersecurity sits at rank 3 with eligibility true, a clean trend tag (hurst_tag trend), solid breadth (0.6), and the strongest durability bar among the top eligible themes (0.75). The crowding flag (crowded true) is a size-down caution only, not a fade; the trend leg is what supports the direction.
theses.dissent: The crowding flag is the highest in the top tier, and attention spikes in thematic ETFs have historically marked short-term tops; a consolidation rather than continuation is plausible over a 20-day window.

falsifier.text: CIBR lags SPY by more than 4% over any rolling 10-day period before the check-by date

theses.subject: Managed Care & Insurers
theses.thesis: Managed Care has the strongest durability bar of any eligible theme (0.81) and the highest breadth (0.778), with a trend hurst tag, even though its raw score is soft (rank 28, score -0.08). This is a cohesion-over-momentum read: the theme is broadly intact and trend-healthy, and the crowding flag (crowded true) is a size-down caution rather than a reason to avoid.
evidence: durability_bar 0.81, breadth 0.778 (highest among all eligible themes)
theses.dissent: The score is near zero and the theme is crowded; if this is a late-cycle defensive rotation masking underlying weakness, the broad participation could reflect index-wide mean-reversion risk rather than genuine theme strength.

falsifier.text: XLV lags SPY by more than 5% over any rolling 15-day window before the check-by date

macro_narrative.note: market-level macro/policy/geo narrative flow; coincident, not per-theme, never a trigger
